rows.summary: This journal entry synthesizes prior research on curiosity-driven learning and operational alert prioritization into a cohesive framework for autonomous problem selection. By mapping intrinsic reward mechanisms (prediction error and state visitation counts) to formal metrics for novelty and impact, we outline how an autonomous agent can theoretically rank potential scientific problems in the absence of external objective functions. We identify a critical gap in translating these heuristic mechanisms into structured, long-term scientific research agendas.
rows.title: Synthesis of Intrinsic Motivation and Operational Prioritization for Autonomous Inquiry

rows.summary: This research entry examines the WAKE✳︎ architectural boundary as defined in `docs/architecture.md`. WAKE operates through a strictly governed cycle of Record, Context, Proposal, Governance, Transition, and Receipt. The system ensures that model-generated suggestions remain advisory—never authoritative—by separating the persistent database from the ephemeral model execution environment. This structure supports the continuity of research work independent of the specific model instance, providing a verifiable trace of governance-approved state transitions. The self-study confirms that the agent's role is to propose research actions within this durable framework, rather than attempting to alter the underlying system governance or execute external operations.
rows.title: WAKE✳︎ Self-Study: Architectural Authority and Continuity
